version.changelog: Set fixed cloud base URL to https://i-sync.cn by default; cloud setup now requires only device_id and token; streamline first-run prompts accordingly.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.2.0

The skill bundle provides web scraping automation for platforms like Douyin and TikTok, utilizing a local bridge or a cloud dispatch service (i-sync.cn). It contains high-risk capabilities, including the execution of arbitrary shell commands via the `--bridge-cmd` argument in `scripts/collect_and_export_loop.sh` and remote code execution via SSH in `scripts/run.sh`. While these features are functionally aligned with the stated purpose of managing a collection connector, the broad execution surface and the handling of user API tokens for an external cloud endpoint (https://i-sync.cn) pose a significant risk of exploitation via prompt injection or unauthorized command execution.

llm.summary: The skill's scripts and instructions match its stated goal (browser-extension data collection), but it requires access to the user's normal Chrome environment, persists a cloud API token locally, and (in cloud mode) will send that token and collection payloads to an external host (https://i-sync.cn) — these privacy/remote-dispatch behaviors merit caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (web collection via local bridge or cloud dispatch) aligns with the shipped scripts: they call a local bridge API (default http://127.0.0.1:19820), can start a bridge process, build collection payloads, and dispatch to a cloud connector. The requirement of curl/node is appropriate. Notable: SKILL.md explicitly instructs using the user's normal Chrome profile (not an isolated profile) which is consistent with browser-extension collection but increases access to sensitive browser data.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts will (a) read/write preferences under $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or $HOME/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json (including storing defaultCloudToken), (b) interact with a local bridge API to start/stop collection and export results, and (c) in cloud mode wrap and forward payloads to the cloud API and poll for command status. The cloud flow will send Authorization: Bearer <token> and collection payloads to the fixed default host https://i-sync.cn. The SKILL.md also instructs using the user's normal Chrome environment, which implies access to cookies, history, and extension state. All of these actions go beyond mere lightweight querying and have privacy/exfiltration implications.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install/download step is declared (instruction-only with bundled scripts). There are no brew/npm/remote downloads. Scripts run locally and require curl/node already on PATH. This is lower-risk from an install-supply-chain perspective, though the included scripts will be executed if you run them.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, but the skill supports and uses environment variables (WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_TOKEN, WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_DEVICE_ID, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, etc.) and will prompt the user for a cloud API token if cloud mode is used. Storing and transmitting that token is functional for cloud dispatch, but you should treat it as a sensitive credential. No unrelated credentials appear to be requested, but the skill persists tokens to disk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does persist preferences under the user's OpenClaw state directory (~/.openclaw by default). It is not always-enabled and does not request platform-wide privileges in metadata. It can run a user-specified bridge command (BRIDGE_CMD) which could run arbitrary processes — normal for this type of connector tooling but powerful, so review what you permit to be started.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement what it claims, but it performs sensitive operations you should consciously accept before installing:

- It instructs using your normal Chrome profile (not an isolated profile). That means any browser cookies, logged-in sessions, history, and extension state accessible via the connector could be used during collection. Only proceed if you understand and permit that level of access.

- Cloud mode requires you to provide an API token (defaultCloudToken / WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_TOKEN). The token is stored in a local preferences file (~/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json) and will be sent as a Bearer token to the cloud dispatch endpoint (default: https://i-sync.cn). Verify and trust that remote domain before giving any tokens. If you do not trust that domain, use local mode only and avoid entering your token.

- The scripts can start a bridge process via a user-supplied command (BRIDGE_CMD). Inspect that command and the scripts before running to ensure no unexpected commands will execute.

- Recommended actions before running/installing:
  - Inspect the full scripts yourself (they are bundled) and search for any hard-coded remote hosts; here the default cloud host is i-sync.cn.
  - Prefer local mode if you want to avoid sending data to an external cloud service.
  - If you must use cloud mode, provide a minimal/ephemeral token, not long-lived primary credentials, and consider rotating it afterward.
  - Consider running the tool in a controlled environment (separate profile or VM) rather than your main Chrome profile to limit exposure.

Given the privacy and remote-dispatch behavior, treat this skill as potentially invasive and proceed only after verifying the cloud operator and reviewing the scripts.
